question.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given below. What is $[x]_{C}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $\mathcal{B}$ to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ and the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}$ are given below. What is $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{C}}?$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14134086/assets/1508508e1c517a6dd13891a68db89b641c418f5f0f792b3822403be11594f561.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{C},$ we find the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to $\mathcal{C}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 \\ 5 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
